title: The Company That Sold 'Eco-Friendly' Cars—Powered by Coal
hook: A car company marketed itself as green while secretly running its factory on a coal plant it owned.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes hypocrisy in sustainability marketing—highly shareable among climate-conscious audiences.

title: The Trader Who Shortened a Stock by Leaking CEO's Secret Affair
hook: He hired a private investigator, leaked the affair to a tabloid, and made millions when the stock crashed.
why_this_can_go_viral: Juicy scandal + financial crime = viral cocktail. Feels like a movie plot.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Funeral Homes—Then Refused to Cremate the Poor
hook: A single corporation now controls 20% of US funeral homes, and their pricing discriminates by postcode.
why_this_can_go_viral: Death + inequality + monopoly triggers visceral anger and curiosity.

title: The Ad Campaign That Used Ring Doorbells to Sell Home Security
hook: Amazon-owned Ring fed camera footage to a marketing team that targeted terrified homeowners with premium ads.
why_this_can_go_viral: Privacy outrage + corporate abuse + familiar product = explosive shareability.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Fresh' Lobster—It Was Frozen 4 Years Ago and Dyed Red
hook: Some 'fresh' lobster in fancy restaurants has been sitting in a freezer since before the pandemic.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross-out factor + restaurant industry betrayal makes diners think twice.

title: The Cosmetic Company That Hid Asbestos in Lipstick for 40 Years
hook: Internal memos showed executives knew about the asbestos—but decided it was 'too expensive' to fix.
why_this_can_go_viral: Personal health risk + corporate negligence + decades-long lie resonates deeply with women.

title: The Company That Paid Street Gangs to Sabotage Its Competitor's Vans
hook: A logistics firm hired gang members to slash tires and set fire to rival delivery trucks in 3 cities.
why_this_can_go_viral: Cartel-level tactics used by a legitimate company—storytelling gold.

title: The Trader Who Manipulated Wheat Prices by Burning 10,000 Acres of Crops
hook: He didn't short the crop—he caused the shortage. Then sold his stockpile at 4x the price.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shock value of literal arson for profit. Feels like a supervillain origin story.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Synthetic Meat'—It Was Just Tofu With Blood Dye
hook: They claimed their 'lab-grown' burger was the future of food—until a lab test found it was 100% soy.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone loves exposing fake food trends—especially with a health/ethics angle.

title: The Monopoly That Owns All the Crematoriums—Then Made Funerals 'Subscription Only'
hook: You can no longer buy a one-time cremation. You must pay a 'lifetime membership'—for a service you use once.
why_this_can_go_viral: Outrageous subscription model on death itself—absurdly dark and shareable.

title: The Spy Who Used Drone Swarms to Map a Rival's Factory Floor Layout
hook: They flew 12 synchronized drones over the roof at night, using thermal cameras to reconstruct the assembly line.
why_this_can_go_viral: Tech-heavy spycraft feels like a Hollywood thriller. Drone enthusiasts love this.

title: The Ad Agency That Used Your Own Photos to Sell Products Back to You
hook: They scraped Instagram, turned your vacation pic into an ad for sunscreen, and billed the brand $50K.
why_this_can_go_viral: Personal privacy violation + familiar platform = viewers fear it could happen to them.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Organic' Vegetables—Grown in a Toxic Waste Spill Zone
hook: The soil was legally 'hazardous waste'—but the vegetables were sold at Whole Foods with an organic label.
why_this_can_go_viral: Trusted organic label vs. toxic reality—perfect anger-fueled share content.

title: The Oil Company That Faked a Spill Cleanup—and Fined Itself $500
hook: They dumped 50,000 gallons of crude, hired actors to 'clean' it for the news, and paid a token fine to themselves.
why_this_can_go_viral: Massive environmental crime + mockery of justice system = viral outrage.

title: The Trader Who Bought a Ghost Town to Influence Property Futures
hook: He purchased an entire abandoned town, then spread rumors of a 'revitalization project' to spike land value.
why_this_can_go_viral: Bizarre, almost comical—yet deeply unethical. Viewers love 'rich guy buys weird thing' stories.

title: The Startup That Was Just a Website and a Rental Tesla—Raised $20M
hook: The CEO leased a Model S, rented a WeWork office, and fooled VCs into thinking he had a fleet of trucks.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable 'fake it till you make it' gone evil—enthusiasts love the audacity.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Ambulance—Then Charged $5,000 for a Band-Aid
hook: A single private equity firm now controls 80% of ambulances in 3 states. The 'surprise billing' is intentional.
why_this_can_go_viral: Healthcare + profit motive + universal fear = high-emotion shareability.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Competitor's Client List by Posing as a Fire Inspector
hook: He wore a fake uniform, walked into the rival agency, and walked out with a binder of every client contract.
why_this_can_go_viral: Old-school con artist energy—viewers love stories of bold, low-tech deception.

title: The Ad Campaign That Targeted People Right After a Breakup—With Full Knowledge
hook: A dating app bought emotional data from therapists' apps to serve desperate ads at the perfect vulnerable moment.
why_this_can_go_viral: Horrifyingly personal exploitation—viewers will feel both creeped out and fascinated.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Premium' Olive Oil—It Was 100% Canola With Green Dye
hook: They added chlorophyll, beta-carotene, and a whisper of real olive oil to fool chemical tests.
why_this_can_go_viral: Universal kitchen staple exposed as fake—everyone has olive oil in their pantry.

title: The Drug Company That Bribed Pharmacists to Push Opioids—With Cash in Briefcases
hook: Pharmacists were given 'bonuses' for every 100 opioid prescriptions filled—no questions asked about the patient.
why_this_can_go_viral: Opioid crisis + cash bribes + medical betrayal = deeply emotional, high-engagement topic.

title: The Company That Bought a Town's Water—Then Sold It Back at 10x the Price
hook: They bought the municipal water rights for pennies, shut down the public well, and started selling bottles from a tap.
why_this_can_go_viral: Water is life—privatizing it feels like ultimate capitalist evil. Instant outrage shares.

title: The Trader Who Faked a Factory Fire to Crash a Competitor's Stock—Then Bought It Cheap
hook: He hired someone to set off a smoke machine near the rival's warehouse, live-tweeted the 'fire,' and bought the dip.
why_this_can_go_viral: Modern, media-savvy crime—combines social media, stock market, and deception in one tight story.
